findings.title: untrusted() does not escape the source attribute
findings.why: The function only defuses closing tags in text, but callers pass repository-controlled paths as source. A path containing a quote or '</untrusted>' can break the opening tag or forge a closing tag, so repository content can escape the data block and be read as instructions.

findings.title: Module path is outside the untrusted block in the summarizer prompt
findings.why: The repository-controlled module path is interpolated into HumanMessage before the <untrusted> block. Directory names can contain newlines or instruction text, so a malicious repository can prompt-inject the summarizer even after the block's closing tag is defused.

findings.title: Package-marker directories larger than 50 files are split
findings.why: The condition requires both len(all_files) <= MAX_MODULE_FILES and not marked_below(path), but never checks has_marker(path). A directory with package.json et al. and more than 50 files therefore falls through to the split branch, contradicting 'whatever its size' and fragmenting package modules.

findings.title: Repo layer cache key ignores skip_paths
findings.why: _key hashes only LAYER_VERSION, tree id and memory_version. Changing skip rules leaves the tree id unchanged, so cached conventions/tree can keep files that should now be skipped (or omit newly included ones), leaking stale/skipped content into the context.

findings.title: Sample excerpt can exceed the token cap for wide characters
findings.why: The slice uses remaining * 4, assuming four characters per token, while estimate_tokens counts each non-ASCII character as a token. A CJK/emoji-heavy file can make the sample several times larger than _SAMPLE_TOKENS, risking context overflow and extra cost.

findings.title: Empty model output is cached as a valid summary
findings.why: summarize(...).strip() can produce the empty string, which is not None. It is then cached and later loaded as a summary, so the module never falls back to stats and is not retried until its files change.

findings.title: Module cache key serialization is ambiguous
findings.why: Paths and blob ids are joined with newline and '=' without escaping. Git paths may contain newlines and '=', so a crafted file set can serialize to the same string as a different set, causing a stale summary to be reused after the module content changes.
